A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same C-PGC research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original C-PGC experiments on retrieval, captioning, grounding, and entailment, together with ablations, defense evaluations, and other appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original C-PGC experimental results, including the main-text evaluations and supplementary results in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same conditional generator, cross-attention components, contrastive and distance losses, positive-sample selection, and text-replacement procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Flickr30K, MSCOCO, RefCOCO+, and SNLI-VE for the same retrieval, captioning, grounding, and entailment tasks. Cross-domain and defense scenarios in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout: GAP and ETU in Tables 1 and 5, ETU in Table 7, and Co-Attack and SGA in Table 10. Figure 2 also retains UAP, PGD-based UAP, and GAP.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B preserve the same splits, sampling counts, augmentations, model configurations, and 40-epoch training. Attack budgets remain 12/255 for images and one replaced word for text; evaluation metrics and appendix procedures also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendices C–F and H retain the same component and loss ablations, budget sensitivity, cross-domain and defense tests, semantic-similarity and alignment analyses, and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: The point-estimate and averaging practices are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental seed identifiers, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted or qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains C-PGC's ALBEF white-box ASRs of 90.13% TR and 88.82% IR; Appendix Table 5 retains ALBEF-to-TCL ASRs of 82.49% TR and 76.24% IR.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain identical attack constraints, cross-attention definitions, losses, training objective, and relative feature-distance definition. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about universal multimodal attacks, disrupting cross-modal alignment, and effectiveness across six VLP models and multiple tasks.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations of transferability, defenses, and semantic similarity are unchanged. Both retain Appendix C's SNLI-VE annotation caveat and Appendix G's limitations concerning perturbation interactions and textual semantic consistency.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–B contain the same pseudocode, training sample counts, noise dimensions, optimizer settings, and other implementation details. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 51 cited works and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to instance-specific attacks, generative universal attacks, and the concurrent ETU method is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, 9 March 2025, to v4, 22 December 2025. Apart from this administrative text and extraction-level spacing differences, the wording, title, authors, headings, and section order match.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–11 retain the same graphics, captions, axes, legends, structures, and placements. Rendered comparisons show no figure or table redesign, relocation, or page-layout revision.

improvement.justification: The later version preserves the same scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and limitations throughout the main text and appendices. The updated arXiv stamp does not meaningfully affect clarity, rigor, or evidential support, leaving overall paper quality unchanged.
